topic_name: The Need for Smaller Units and the Tenth

item.question: A ruler has every centimetre split into 10 equal parts. One screw ends 7 parts after the 2 cm mark and another ends 2 parts after the 3 cm mark. Write each length and say what the first one means.
steps: The first screw is more than 2 1/2 cm but less than 3 cm, so it lies between 2 cm and 3 cm.
The unit between two consecutive numbers is divided into 10 equal parts, so each part is 1/10 cm.
From 0 we go to 2, then take 7 parts of 1/10: the length is 2 cm and 7/10 cm, that is 2 7/10 cm.
In the same way the second screw is 3 cm and 2/10 cm, that is 3 2/10 cm.
item.answer: First screw 2 7/10 cm, second screw 3 2/10 cm

topic_name: The Need for Smaller Units and the Tenth
concept_name: A tenth part: two ways to write a length

item.question: A pencil is 3 4/10 units long. Write its length as a count of tenths and show why it is the same length.
steps: 10 one-tenths make 1 unit, so 3 units is 3 × 10 = 30 tenths.
30 tenths and 4 tenths make 34 tenths, so the length is 34/10 units.
item.text:
Worked example: A pencil is 3 4/10 units long. Write its length as a count of tenths and show why it is the same length.
1. 10 one-tenths make 1 unit, so 3 units is 3 × 10 = 30 tenths.
2. 30 tenths and 4 tenths make 34 tenths, so the length is 34/10 units.
3. Check: 34/10 = 10/10 + 10/10 + 10/10 + 4/10, and each 10/10 is 1 unit, so that is 1 + 1 + 1 + 4/10 = 3 4/10.
Answer: 34/10 units

concept_name: A tenth part: two ways to write a length

item.question: A USB cable is 4 8/10 units long. Write it in two ways. Then read aloud 4 1/10, 4/10, 41/10 and 41 1/10. Three more objects are drawn on their own unit scales: a hand that reaches 1 unit and 6 tenths, a box that is 2 units and 3 tenths, and a leaf that is 3 units and 9 tenths. Write each of these in two ways.
steps: USB cable: 4 units and 8 tenths is 4 8/10, and 4 × 10 + 8 = 48 tenths, so 48/10.
4 1/10 is four and one-tenth; 4/10 is four-tenths; 41/10 is forty-one tenths; 41 1/10 is forty-one and one-tenth.
item.text:

2. 4 1/10 is four and one-tenth; 4/10 is four-tenths; 41/10 is forty-one tenths; 41 1/10 is forty-one and one-tenth.
3. Hand: 1 6/10, and 1 × 10 + 6 = 16 tenths, so 16/10.
4. Box: 2 3/10, and 2 × 10 + 3 = 23 tenths, so 23/10.
5. Leaf: 3 9/10, and 3 × 10 + 9 = 39 tenths, so 39/10.

item.question: Along a ruler marked in tenths of a centimetre, an eraser ends 4 parts after the 2 cm mark, a pencil ends 5 parts after the 4 cm mark and a chalk ends 4 parts after the 1 cm mark. Write each length.
steps: Each part is 1/10 cm, so we read units first and then the parts.
Eraser: 2 cm and 4 parts, so 2 4/10 cm.
Pencil: 4 cm and 5 parts, so 4 5/10 cm, which is also 4 1/2 cm because 5/10 is half.
Chalk: 1 cm and 4 parts, so 1 4/10 cm.

item.question: Arrange these lengths in increasing order: 4 1/10, 4/10, 41/10 and 41 1/10.
steps: As counts of tenths they are 41, 4, 41 and 411.

The biggest is 41 1/10, which is 411 tenths.

item.question: Sonu's lower arm is 2 7/10 units and his upper arm is 3 6/10 units. What is the total length of his arm? Add in the two ways.
steps: 63/10 is 60/10 + 3/10, which is 6 units and 3 tenths, so 6 3/10 again.
item.text:
Worked example: Sonu's lower arm is 2 7/10 units and his upper arm is 3 6/10 units. What is the total length of his arm? Add in the two ways.
1. Units: 2 + 3 = 5. Tenths: 7/10 + 6/10 = 13/10.
2. 13 tenths is 1 unit and 3 tenths, so 5 + 13/10 = 5 + 10/10 + 3/10 = 5 + 1 + 3/10 = 6 3/10.
3. In tenths: 2 7/10 is 27/10 and 3 6/10 is 36/10, and 27/10 + 36/10 = 63/10.
4. 63/10 is 60/10 + 3/10, which is 6 units and 3 tenths, so 6 3/10 again.
Answer: 6 3/10 units

item.question: Shylaja's hand is 12 4/10 units long and her palm is 6 7/10 units. How long is her middle finger? Solve it by breaking a unit, and check by converting to tenths.
steps: There are only 4 tenths in the hand, and 7 tenths must be taken away.
Break 1 unit of the 12 into 10 tenths: 12 4/10 becomes 11 14/10.
14 tenths − 7 tenths = 7 tenths, and 11 units − 6 units = 5 units, so 5 7/10.
item.text:
Worked example: Shylaja's hand is 12 4/10 units long and her palm is 6 7/10 units. How long is her middle finger? Solve it by breaking a unit, and check by converting to tenths.
1. There are only 4 tenths in the hand, and 7 tenths must be taken away.
2. Break 1 unit of the 12 into 10 tenths: 12 4/10 becomes 11 14/10.
3. 14 tenths − 7 tenths = 7 tenths, and 11 units − 6 units = 5 units, so 5 7/10.
4. Check in tenths: 124/10 − 67/10 = 57/10 = 5 7/10.
Answer: 5 7/10 units

item.question: A paper strip 8 9/10 units long is folded in half. Its new length ends between 4 4/10 and 4 5/10. Split each tenth into 10 parts: what is one small part, and where does the folded strip end? Can the length also be said as 4 units and 45 hundredths?
steps: Each tenth has 10 smaller parts and a unit has 10 tenths, so a unit has 10 × 10 = 100 smaller parts.
One part is 1/100 of a unit.
The folded strip ends 5 parts after the 4 4/10 mark, so it is 4 units and 4 tenths and 5 hundredths.
10 hundredths make 1 tenth, so 4 tenths is 40 hundredths, and 40 + 5 = 45 hundredths.
So yes, the length is also 4 units and 45 hundredths, that is 4 45/100.

Worked example: Four rulers show lengths in hundredths: one reaches 37 parts after the 5 mark, another 3 parts after the 15 mark, another 52 parts after the 7 mark and the last 80 parts after the 9 mark. Write each measurement and read it in words.
1. 37 parts after 5: 5 37/100, read 'five and thirty-seven hundredths'.
2. 3 parts after 15: 15 3/100, read 'fifteen and three hundredths'.
3. 52 parts after 7: 7 52/100, read 'seven and fifty-two hundredths'.
4. 80 parts after 9: 9 80/100, read 'nine and eighty hundredths'.
Answer: 5 37/100, 15 3/100, 7 52/100, 9 80/100

maths_rules: 37 parts after the 5 mark is 5 and 37 hundredths, 5 37/100.
3 parts after the 15 mark is 15 and 3 hundredths, 15 3/100; the 3 sits in the hundredths place, not as 30.
52 parts after the 7 mark is 7 52/100.
80 parts after the 9 mark is 9 80/100, read nine and eighty hundredths.
Slip: 37 small parts are not 37 tenths, because a unit has only 10 tenths.
